These are consolidation and release-prep edits; no executable code, wire protocol, crypto or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence, so no concrete security regression is identified.

Observed behavior: the new v0.10.1 candidate header and upgrade notes are only visible in the patch excerpt, which is truncated; the numbered head text covers older historical sections. The upgrade notes say a coordinator including darkbloom-platform#411 is needed to refuse logprobs on GLM/MiMo/Nemotron before reservation, otherwise a 0.10.0 provider fails the request with 500 generation_failure and cools every provider of the model (availability, TB-002/ADV-002). That is an external contract and an operational dependency outside the supplied evidence, not a regression introduced here. The notes also say the libs/mlx-swift-lm pin moves, which cannot be verified from these units.

Removed fragments describe Autopilot placements/downloads/holds/watchdog, the desktop control API (loopback, authenticated, separate read-only dashboard session), and the console desktop sign-in purpose. The fragments' content presumably moves into CHANGELOG.md, but the supplied excerpts are truncated, so whether the removal drops those entries is unverified. T-041 prefix-cache statements in changelog entries (encrypted SSD default, 100 GiB ceiling limited to half the available space) are historical records. They are consistent with the T-041 sign-off wording about the available-disk/2 budget with no fixed ceiling, but a 100 GiB default ceiling versus 'no fixed ceiling' in the threat model may be a documentation drift worth checking against code. That is pre-existing and not part of this diff's added lines.

Remaining integration questions: confirm that the fragments' security-relevant claims (desktop loopback API auth, Autopilot downloads default-on) are in code changed elsewhere in this PR and whether the threat model needs updating for those surfaces.
